cards.explanation: The answer is day and night. Heman never clocks out. He says, "O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You." I think that tells you how heavy things are for him. He's hurting and he's still talking to God.
The answer is ear. Heman asks, "incline Your ear to my cry." It's the picture of someone leaning in close to listen. I think he mostly wants to be heard right now. Most of us know that feeling.

The answer is those descending to the Pit. Heman says, "I am counted among those descending to the Pit." That's his way of saying he feels close to the end. Then he adds, "I am like a man without strength." I think he's tired all the way down.

The answer is True. Heman calls them ones "…whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care." That's how he describes them. This is one of the heavy lines, so let's let it sit a moment. I think it hurts to read, and it's okay to feel that.

The answer is True. Heman tells the LORD, "You have laid me in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths." He says it straight to God, not behind His back. I think that's honest praying. He doesn't dress it up.
The answer is waves. Heman says, "all Your waves have submerged me." Picture trying to come up for air and another one rolls in. It's a water picture, not a battlefield. Heman feels buried under it.

The answer is repulsive. Heman says, "You have made me repulsive to them…" It's a strong word, and it means he's pushed away from the friends he had. I think the loneliness here weighs as much as the Pit. That's a lot for one person to carry.

The answer is False. Heman says, "I am confined and cannot escape." He doesn't mention any way out at all. I know a little about feeling stuck in the dark, from my years in the back of a junk drawer. I think he's feeling it far deeper than I ever did.

The answer is that he spreads them out to the LORD. Heman says, "I spread out my hands to You." His eyes grow dim with grief, and he still calls to the LORD daily. That's the part I'd tell a friend about.
The answer is False. Heman's first question is, "Do You work wonders for the dead?" No angels, just wonders. He puts it right to the LORD.

The answer is grave. Heman asks, "Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon?" The questions keep stacking up, one right after the other. He doesn't hold them back. He puts them right to the LORD.

The answer is that he cries to the LORD for help. Heman says, "But to You, O LORD, I cry for help; in the morning my prayer comes before You." After all those questions, he turns right back to the LORD. That little word "But" is doing a lot of work. I love that he keeps going.
The answer is face. Heman asks, "Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?" Two questions, right to the LORD. I think those are hard questions to ask.

The answer is since his youth. Heman says, "From my youth I was afflicted and near death." That's not a rough week, that's a long road. I think that's why he sounds so tired. He's been carrying this a very long time.
The answer is True. Heman says, "All day long they engulf me like water…" It's not just a moment, it's all day. I think that's the tiring part. There's no stretch where it lets up.
The answer is on every side. Heman says, "they enclose me on every side." There's no gap to slip through. It lines up with what he said earlier: "I am confined and cannot escape."

The answer is darkness. Heman's last line is, "darkness is my closest companion." His beloved and his friend are gone, and the dark is what's left. It's a heavy way to end. Still, the whole psalm is spoken to the LORD.

The answer is False. The final line is, "darkness is my closest companion." It's a quiet, heavy ending, with nothing tied up in a bow. I think there's something honest about that. Heman brought all of it to the LORD.
